correctness.rationale: For Δ(2,n) the Ehrhart function equals binom(2k+n−1,n−1)−n binom(k+n−2,n−1), since at most one coordinate exceeds k. Backward differences give degree v=2^(n−1)−n and sectional genus g=1+(n−4)2^(n−3), hence Hurwitz h=n(2^(n−2)−2). Positive-dimensional torus orbits are smooth; each of binom(n,2) singular vertices has local 2×(n−2) rank-one determinantal Segre cone. For generic vertex coefficient ε, a generic local transverse system has m=n−2 simple nearby branches with linear leading ε scales, evaluation determinant leading ε^(m−1) times a nonzero Cauchy/interpolation determinant; its trace-pairing discriminant contributes 2(m−1)=2(n−3). Subtract these vertex exponents from coefficient degree (n−1)h to obtain b=n(n−1)(2^(n−2)−n+1). Independent exact integer degree and Ehrhart checks confirm (b,h)=(12,8),(80,30),(330,84),(1092,210) for n=4–7; the general local argument, not the numeric table, bears the unrestricted proof.
